Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (MAP will follow)

Hi Sabrina —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to seed the MAP draft:

Key requirements we heard
- Low-latency text generation for customer support routing (95th pctl < 300ms)
- On-prem/private deployment option for PII-sensitive workloads
- Cost target: average token cost reduction compared to current setup (~30%)
- Success criteria: pilot supporting 10k monthly chats with <1% error rate and ability to scale to 100k

Primary stakeholders
- Sabrina Lee (Acme) — project lead / product owner
- Tom Wu (Acme) — infra & procurement lead
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — AE / commercial lead
- Rachel Kim (Redwood) — Customer Success / onboarding
- Dev Patel (Redwood) — Solutions / SRE for deployment plan

Next steps I’ll drive from Redwood:
1) Send MAP draft with milestones, owners, target close and go-live window (ETA Mon 3/1)
2) Share proposed pricing & term sheet for procurement review (attached to MAP)
3) Kick off technical scoping call (Rachel & Dev) once Acme confirms target go-live window

Please reply with any corrections to the above. If 3/1 for the MAP draft works for you I’ll ping that over first thing Mon.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Sabrina / Tom —

Attached is the initial Mutual Action Plan (v1.1) based on our discovery and the notes below. High level milestones, target dates and owners are captured on tab "Milestones." Please review and comment — I’ll incorporate and send a final by 3/12 if we’re aligned.

Highlights (see attached Acme_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx)
- Target signature date: 2026-03-12 (Rationale: gives procurement/legal time to review; Redwood committed to provisioning dedicated capacity by 3/20)
- Target go-live window: 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-07 (post-integration smoke tests)
- Critical path items:
  - Legal review & SLA approval (Tom / Acme Legal) — due 2026-03-08
  - Procurement PO & contract signature (Procurement) — due 2026-03-12
  - Technical validation (integration, SSO, network/IP allowlist) — due 2026-03-22
- Owners assigned in column B; dependencies are listed in column D.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Are you okay with the proposed signature date 3/12 or do you need more procurement lead time?
2) Do you want Redwood to provision a short-lived dedicated pool for the pilot, or begin on hosted with a switch to dedicated at go-live? (we typically recommend dedicated for predictable latency)

Attachments included:
- Acme_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones, owners, acceptance criteria)
- Pricing_Term_Sheet.pdf (summary pricing & optional commitments)
- SLA_Redwood_v1.pdf (standard SLA we propose)

If it helps, happy to run a 30-min alignment call this week to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the thoroughness. Quick notes from our side after an initial review:

- Procurement note: 3/12 signature looks tight. We may need until 3/19 to get internal PO approvals (legal is booked next week). Can we push the signature target to 3/19?
- Technical: We prefer to start the pilot on hosted with strict allowlist and then shift to dedicated for production. That reduces provisioning lead time. Can you reflect that option in the MAP?
- SLA: We need a clause about data residency for PII flows — is that included in SLA_Redwood_v1? If not, please flag how Redwood handles PII in private deployments.

Small edits I made in the MAP (see inline comments in Acme_MAP_Draft_v2.xlsx).

If it's helpful, I can schedule procurement checkpoints on 3/10 and 3/17.

Tom

2) Decision on pilot approach (hosted->dedicated or direct dedicated)
3) Confirmation that Tom’s team can provide SSO certs and allowlist IPs by 3/18
